title: Plain early jazz trumpet versus the fancy style
summary: Early jazz trumpet was played straight, like Big Landry, until Chris Kelly's generation brought the fancy style.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Oh, Sam. Well, the music then was good. But as it kept coming, coming, coming, the fellas got better and better.
Yeah. Jazz used to be on a style that nobody had all that fancy playing on their trumpet.

They played straight and things. But during the time when Chris Kelly and all of them got together and all, stopped playing, well, that's when the fancy trumpet come in. Yeah. You know, making all the different things. Yeah. But before they used to play straight, they used to play just like Big Landry. Oh, yes. Landry would die. And he never did change his way. He said that same way when what they played way back.
You used to hear him down in Lutzen's with Big Eye.
Yeah. That's the way he played. Never did change his style of playing. But Randy Howard, all them boys, they come on up to the right. They boost up the jazz. And went good too.
